solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nick is essential to plan to support one in charge

indicators.note: being essential to something here means sitting at its heart, so the word is goes into the middle

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart
a prop is a support or buttress

indicators.note: one is placed within the word for charge

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A sentence about how a petty theft is central to a scheme backing whoever is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for steal, not a notch or a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for taking something dishonestly; nick is informal British slang for stealing.

clue.text: Close up in group, one from the Eighties

indicators.note: the reversed word for close sits inside the word for group

parts.note: a mass is a large group or number

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to end is to close or finish

explanation.surface: Instructions to bunch together in a group, like a band member from the 1980s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' is the verb, to finish, not the adjective meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness was a British ska-pop band with many hits in the early 1980s, so the band is one example from that decade.

clue.text: Results of marathon perhaps break, with anxiety to come first and second

indicators.note: the word for anxiety is told to come before the word for break

parts.note: stress is anxiety or strain
a fracture is a break

explanation.surface: Runners' injuries after a long race, with worry arriving first and second.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairline cracks in bone from repeated impact are typical injuries of long-distance running, so a marathon is one cause.

clue.text: Dial former illustrator

definitions.meaning: dial is old slang for a face, and so is this word
the pen name of Hablot K. Browne, who illustrated Dickens's novels

explanation.surface: A clock face and an old artist, a two-word puzzle of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for the human face, and the same word was the pseudonym of the Victorian illustrator of Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Melancholy rake choked up when all sign of love is lost

indicators.text: when all sign of love is lost
indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, and every such letter is dropped

parts.note: a roue is a rake, a dissolute man
to foul up is to clog or choke

explanation.surface: A womaniser is too emotional to speak once the romance has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Joining ROUE and FOUL gives ROUEFOUL; dropping both O letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe a sorrowful, regretful mood.

clue.text: Order for taxi to collect drink?

definitions.meaning: what you might say to a cab firm wanting a ride from your door

explanation.surface: Ringing for a cab to fetch some alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic that revives you is called by this phrase, and the same words are a request for a cab to fetch you.

clue.text: Bombed Britain, having been shelled, needs to be rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilding puts these letters back together in a new order
shelling removes the outer casing, leaving the inner letters

explanation.surface: A wartime picture of a blitzed country needing reconstruction.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelling 'needs' leaves EED; BRITAIN plus EED rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombed is slang for very drunk, so it shares the sense of intoxicated.

clue.text: Artwork in article with delivery from non-European locations

parts.note: the definite article
a birth is a delivery of a baby
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent

indicators.note: dropping E, the abbreviation for European

parts.note: venues are locations

explanation.surface: A painting shown in a magazine piece about babies delivered from places outside Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Botticelli's famous painting of the goddess rising from the sea is a celebrated Renaissance artwork.

clue.text: Listen for what may follow news on daughter

parts.note: the BBC programme News at Ten gives the words that follow news

explanation.surface: Pay attention to what comes after the bulletin about your daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a long-running British evening TV news programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay heed or give ear is the old sense, as in attend to my words.

clue.text: They will hibernate in a room that is cold to enter

parts.note: a dorm is a dormitory, a sleeping room

indicators.note: the letter for cold goes into the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: Creatures heading for a chilly room to sleep through winter.
explanation.definitionFit: These small rodents are famous for their long winter sleep.

clue.text: Kind of fruit reduced by 30 per cent

indicators.note: being reduced by a share means that much is cut off the end of the word for fruit

parts.note: a clementine is a small citrus fruit
thirty per cent of the ten-letter fruit is its last three letters, the part cut away

explanation.surface: A type of fruit marked down by thirty per cent, like a shop offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like it means type of, but 'Kind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful or gentle, a synonym for kind.

clue.text: Ultimately, The Obama Diaries advocate freedom

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A former president's memoirs argue the case for liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease means freedom from difficulty or constraint, as in ill at ease.

clue.text: Adder having a stretch when it's warm

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, an adder of figures
a stretch is a period of time

explanation.surface: A snake stretching out in the warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' is not the snake but a person who adds.
explanation.definitionFit: The warm season of the year is the hot months.

clue.text: Bouncers may work on it

parts.note: bouncers suggests nightclub doormen, but here it means people who bounce on a springy frame

explanation.surface: Door staff at their workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut fabric sheet on springs is where gymnasts and children bounce.

clue.text: Hunt in South Africa, avoiding Cape when touring

indicators.note: touring means moving around, so the letters travel into a new order
avoiding means the letter for cape is left out

explanation.surface: A game hunt on a trip through South Africa that skips the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when touring' signals the anagram of the shortened country, which follows S.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedition to hunt or watch wild animals, especially in Africa.

clue.text: Played in the wrong order, being eclipsed

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrasal verb swap places

parts.note: acted out means played or performed

explanation.surface: A performance done in the wrong sequence, upstaged by others.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surpassed on stage by a fellow performer is to be overshadowed or eclipsed.

clue.text: Hero's weapon overcoming destiny

indicators.note: in a down clue the weapon sits over, above, the word for destiny

parts.note: a lance is a knight's weapon
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A hero's sword or spear defeating fate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian knight is the hero of many romances.

clue.text: Could one in trouble be this utterly chicken?

definitions.text: Could one in trouble be this

parts.note: dead is informal for utterly, as in dead gorgeous
chicken is an example of meat

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone in a fix is completely cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' seems to mean cowardly but is the poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in serious trouble is said to be doomed, finished, with this slang phrase.

clue.text: Order soldiers to stop tyrant — not half

indicators.note: the soldiers plug the gap, sitting inside the shortened tyrant
only half the word for tyrant is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: a dictator is a tyrant
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Commanding troops to halt a despot, with a sly 'not half' of emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: To order is to command or instruct, a verb sense.

clue.text: He was gloomy about going after every job when regularly rejected

indicators.note: the word for about comes after the kept letters
every other letter is thrown out, keeping the first, third and so on

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A man despondent after one job application after another was turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: The donkey in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh is famously gloomy and pessimistic.

clue.text: Dead former law passed by Parliament has lobby disheartened

parts.note: ex means former
an act is a statute passed by Parliament

indicators.note: the heart of the word is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An old law, once lobbied for, now defunct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead' is the adverb, as in dead right, not lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead as an adverb means precisely, as in dead on time.

clue.text: Nomadic worker suppressed by mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue the worker is held below the word for mistake

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A wandering labourer held down by an error.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering or roving, as in a knight errant.

clue.text: Helping Jack, say, to obtain share certificates?

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion
a jack is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: Helping a man named Jack to get his stock documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'share certificates' suggests stocks, but here they are documents entitling you to a share of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime coupons allowed each holder a fixed share of scarce food, so they certify a share.

clue.text: In a certain type of light, each is a bit of a looker

parts.note: UV is ultraviolet light

explanation.surface: Under some kind of lighting, everyone looks attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looker' seems to mean a beauty, but it is an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigmented layer of the eye including the iris is part of the organ that looks.

clue.text: Gangster boss promoted old man in 'the Firm'

indicators.note: the reversed father goes inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: in a down clue promoted means moved up, written bottom to top

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A mobster chief advancing a veteran within his criminal organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Mafia a capo heads a crew of soldiers, a gang leader.

clue.text: Warm drink

definitions.meaning: warm here means friendly and heartfelt

explanation.surface: A hot beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means friendly and also names a sweetened fruit drink diluted with water.

clue.text: Touching progress, in a way

indicators.note: the word for progress sits inside a and the word for way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to gain is to progress or advance

explanation.surface: Moving and making headway, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Against can mean in contact with, as in leaning against a wall.

clue.text: Circulation booster needs cover that's redesigned so I lay out in an OTT style

indicators.note: the circulation booster is wrapped by the rearranged letters
redesigned means the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: a stent is a tube inserted to keep a blood vessel open

explanation.surface: A medical device needing a redesigned casing, so a patient can lie back in flashy fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: SO I LAY OUT rearranged to OATIOUSLY wraps round STENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something showily or flamboyantly is acting over the top.
